title: Inquest called in Taser death case
article: Tasers will be put to the test this spring when Ontario holds its first inquest into a death involving the powerful stun guns.

The probe will focus not only on the May 2004 death of London resident Peter Lamonday -- who died minutes after being shot by city police with a Taser -- but also on the overall controversy around the weapon, Ontario's deputy chief coroner said.
"Certainly the use of Tasers is in the public view and it's quite controversial," Dr. Bonita Porter said Tuesday after announcing the May 2 inquest.
"We're hopeful (the inquest's jury) can make appropriate recommendations about the continued use of Tasers."
Seven London police officers were cleared by the province's police watchdog last summer in the death of Lamonday, a 33-year-old landscaper who had cocaine in his system the night of his death.
It was the drugs, not the police actions or stun gun, that killed him, the investigation concluded.
No death has ever been directly attributed to a Taser.

But the safety of the weapon, which briefly immobilizes a person with a 50,000-volt jolt, isn't so clear to Lamonday's still- grieving girlfriend. "It's been a long struggle for me without answers," said Cathy Colborne.
